negative_findings.description: No bank-published shareholder general-assembly notices ('njoftim për kuvendin e aksionarëve', 'ftesë për mbledhjen e përgjithshme të aksionarëve') were located for any Kosovo commercial bank, in Albanian or Serbian.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Albanian-language query returned only the Law on Business Organizations (Ligji për Shoqëritë Tregtare) as published via ARBK/MINT and unrelated 2025 political items — no actual bank convocation notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Kosovo's banks are unlisted, so there is no exchange-disclosure obligation forcing convocation notices onto a public feed. The shareholder-governance layer of workstream A1 therefore has to be reconstructed from the company registry (ARBK) and from annual-report governance chapters, not from an IR notices feed. Collection design should not assume this feed exists.

negative_findings.description: No Serbian-language ('sr') disclosure channel was found on ANY Kosovo commercial bank's own website. The sr-language search returned only Serbia-domiciled sister banks (procreditbank.rs, nlbkb.rs), NBS's Serbian bank-balance-sheet portal, and CBK's own ?lang=sr pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian-language hits for 'godišnji izveštaj / revidirani finansijski izveštaji' resolved to Serbia, Montenegro or the Kosovo regulator — not to Kosovo bank IR pages. Kosovo bank IR appears to be sq + en only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The sr-language requirement for this cell can only be met at the regulator layer, not the bank-own layer, and there is a real risk of mis-attributing Serbia-domiciled ProCredit/NLB filings to their Kosovo namesakes. Entity disambiguation rules (domain + legal entity name) are mandatory in the collector.

negative_findings.description: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo's disclosure documents are effectively absent from search indexes; only the container page /en/financial-statements/ was found, with a call-centre phone number and info@teb-kos.com as the stated route to more information.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two separate queries (bank-name and domain-scoped exact-phrase) returned no TEB annual report or audited statement PDF. A paywalled aggregator (The Banker Database) held TEB Kosovo data instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: TEB is a major Kosovo bank; if its own channel is JS-rendered or gated, a plain HTTP scraper will silently produce a coverage hole for one of the largest institutions. Requires a rendering fetcher and an explicit completeness check.

negative_findings.description: No financial reports or disclosure section were located for PriBank Sh.A. (pribank-ks.com) or İŞBANK Kosova (isbankkosova.com) via sq or en search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries returned other banks' reports plus the licensed-bank roster; nothing bank-own for either institution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the two smallest/newest licensed banks. Their absence from the own-disclosure layer means market-total reconstruction from bank-own sources alone will be incomplete and must be closed with CBK aggregate data.

negative_findings.description: The Kosovo Banking Association's own canonical domain could not be confirmed. The seed-implied bankassoc-kos.com did not appear in any search result.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only a member bank's descriptive page (bkt-ks.com) and an official Facebook page surfaced for 'Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The association is the natural aggregation point for sector-level positions and member lists; without its canonical site, that layer depends on social media and second-hand pages. The domain must be resolved before it is trusted — it is recorded here as unconfirmed, not as dead.

negative_findings.description: Multiple host variants serve the same NLB Kosovo documents (nlb-kos.com, www.nlb-kos.com, hr.nlb-kos.com), and Banka Ekonomike serves its archive from two path families after an apparent CMS migration (/Articles/68/Images/... and /wp-content/uploads/...).
negative_findings.result_summary: Identical or near-identical PDFs are reachable under several hosts/paths; some legacy links surfaced only via third-party document mirrors (yumpu, vdocuments) rather than the bank domain.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without canonicalisation the corpus will double-count reports and produce false 'new disclosure' events; third-party mirrors must never be treated as primary because their fidelity is unverified.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language coverage of the bank-own disclosure layer is effectively zero; only the regulator publishes in sr.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm by direct site crawl (not search) whether any Kosovo bank offers an /sr or /srb locale; if not, record sr coverage for this cell as satisfied at the regulator layer only, and document the exclusion explicitly in the source register.

coverage_gaps.description: Three of ten licensed banks (TEB, PriBank, İŞBANK Kosova) have no confirmed retrievable own-channel report set, including one systemically significant institution.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a rendering-browser crawl of teb-kos.com, pribank-ks.com and isbankkosova.com in both sq and en; if still empty, fall back to CBK supervisory aggregates and parent-group segment reporting, and flag these entities as aggregate-only in the register.

coverage_gaps.description: Disclosure cadence is wildly uneven across the cell: ProCredit and Ziraat publish quarterly, most others only annually, and several archives observed here stop at 2023.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Set per-source polling cadence individually rather than one global schedule, and add a staleness alarm per bank (e.g. flag if no new document within 15 months of fiscal year end) so a silently broken crawler is distinguishable from a bank that simply publishes late.

coverage_gaps.description: No bank-own press-release / news feed was systematically mapped for this cell; only Raiffeisen's media/lajme section and NLB's ankande-publike were incidentally identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a second discovery pass targeting 'lajme', 'njoftime', 'media', 'komunikata për media' paths on all ten bank domains, since product launches and payments-strategy signals appear there long before the annual report.

coverage_gaps.description: The shareholder/general-assembly dimension of workstream A1 has no confirmed public feed anywhere in the cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test ARBK per-entity lookups for the ten licensed banks to see whether assembly decisions and capital changes are retrievable, and in parallel extract governance chapters from annual-report PDFs as the fallback evidence base.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs here were surfaced through search snippets rather than fetched, and one 2026-dated CBK register PDF path was inferred from a search result title.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every URL in this slice before promotion; treat any 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than death, and re-resolve 404s from each site's own listing page rather than dropping the source.

brief: Kosovo's commercial banks are all unlisted joint-stock companies, so there is no exchange-disclosure feed and no true 'investor relations' function — the primary-source layer is each bank's own 'Për ne / Publikimet financiare / Pasqyrat financiare' section, in Albanian first and English second. Coverage is strong but uneven: ProCredit and Ziraat publish quarterly, Raiffeisen, NLB, BKT Kosova, Banka Ekonomike and BpB publish audited annual reports and IFRS/CBK statement sets with deep archives (Banka Ekonomike back to 2003), while TEB, PriBank and İŞBANK Kosova exposed no retrievable own-channel documents in this pass. Serbian-language disclosure exists only at the regulator (CBK ?lang=sr), never on bank websites, and Serbia-domiciled ProCredit and NLB sister banks are a live entity-confusion hazard. The two structural substitutes for the missing IR layer are the CBK licensed-institution register plus supervisory reporting templates, and the listed parent groups (RBI, NLB, ProCredit Holding, BKT Albania, İşbank, Ziraat), whose segment reporting often carries Kosovo strategy signals earlier and in more detail than the local subsidiary.
